questions.prompt: Order the simplification of a large transistor schematic down to a familiar stage. Each step after the first uses the result of the step before it.
questions.explanation: Most transistors in a large schematic set bias. Treating a constant gate-source device as a short would ground a signal node. A diode-connected device is an AC ground at its gate, not a signal transistor. The fold node is a low-impedance current sum, not another gain node. Once the current divider is close to one, the gain that remains is about \(-g_m R_L\).
steps: Trace the signal from the input device to the output node, and mark every other device as support.
Diode-connected bias devices only set DC voltages, so treat those nodes as AC grounds.
A device whose gate-source voltage is held constant is a current source: an open circuit at AC, or its \(r_o\) if that resistance matters.
What remains is a known stage. In a folded stack it is a common-source device feeding a common-gate device of the opposite type.

questions.prompt: A worked solution models the bias devices whose gate-source voltage is constant in a folded cascode. Exactly one step is wrong.
questions.explanation: Signal current cannot enter a fixed gate-source device through its gate. The drain node stays in the circuit, loaded only by \(r_o\) when that matters. Shorting the drain to ground would kill the signal at the fold or at the output. A diode-connected transistor is the one whose gate is an AC ground. Leaving the device in as a second common-source stage invents a gain it does not have.
steps: Those gates are tied to fixed bias, so the gate-source voltage does not move with the signal.
With that voltage fixed, the device current has no signal part from the gate.
At AC the device is a current source: an open circuit, or \(r_o\) from its drain to AC ground if that resistance matters.
A constant current is a short circuit to AC ground, so replace each of those drains with a short.
reasons: A current source is an open circuit at AC. A short would be a voltage source or a diode-connected gate.
Fixed gate-source voltage means the device is off, so both the current source and \(r_o\) should be deleted.

questions.prompt: Write the resistance seen looking into the source of the common-gate device in a folded cascode. Its drain sees its own output resistance in series with the load RL, and its gate is at AC ground. Use ro3, RL, and gm3.
questions.explanation: The source resistance is \((r_{o3}+R_L)/(1+g_{m3}r_{o3})\). When the load is only a few times \(1/g_m\) and \(g_m r_o\) is large, this is about \(1/g_{m3}\). It rises once the load becomes comparable to \(g_{m3}r_{o3}\), and the \(1/g_m\) shortcut then fails. \(1/g_{m3}\) alone drops the load. \(r_{o3}+R_L\) is the series string without the source factor. The current divider at the fold uses \(g_{m3}\), \(1/r_{o1}\), and \(1/r_{o2}\); it is not this input resistance.
